names: P23 -- landscaped plaza and lawn (north of the pavilion, toward Chase Center)
summary: A landscaped lawn and plaza north of the Mission Creek Park Pavilion, extending toward the Chase Center roundabout; real landscaped/paved open land per satellite imagery, delineated by this project's owner-directed real-gap-fragment method rather than a surveyed parcel boundary. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P23' among the parcels already managed by the Port of San Francisco (not among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), consistent with it being complete by that date. Name and specific operator not confirmed by any source found.

milestones.text: Already part of the Port of San Francisco's managed open-space inventory (not listed among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), per OCII's Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation to the Mission Bay CAC -- an upper bound on when this area was built, not its actual construction date

sources.title: Mission Bay Parks Open Space (CAC Item 2, September 2023)
sources.publisher: Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (sfocii.org)

open_questions: No source names this specific lawn/plaza or gives its own construction date; the Sept 2023 OCII document only establishes it existed and was already Port-managed by that date, which is an upper bound, not a build date.

It sits adjacent to the Chase Center arena (opened September 2019, per this repo's own record 8722025) and to the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision / 499 Illinois St area, but no source ties this landscaped area's own completion to either project.

Whether OCII's own current numbering scheme still uses 'P23' for exactly this footprint was not independently confirmed -- OCII's current public Mission Bay South open-space page (sfocii.org/projects/mission-bay-south/open-space) does not list a P23 at all among the parcels it names (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6, P26).
